input:
The settler sized in this case has a plan area of 294 m2. The area is derived from the design overflow rate and the throughput, and it stands or falls with the overflow rate adopted.

The design overflow rate is 0.51 m h-1 at a throughput of 150 m3 h-1. The plan area follows from the throughput divided by the overflow rate, 150 / 0.51, which yields the stated 294 m2; the overflow rate is the sizing quantity, and the area is whatever the throughput requires at that rate. In operation, sand is removed by gravity settling across that area: the stream passes over the plan area at the design rate, and the sand that settles during the pass is drawn from the bottom of the unit while the clarified stream leaves over the outlet. A larger throughput at the same overflow rate would require the area in direct proportion, and a smaller overflow rate at the same throughput more area in inverse proportion; the stated area belongs to the stated pairing of rate and throughput and to no other.

The overflow rate rests on a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, and the figure has not been checked against the behaviour of the sand in the actual stream: particle size distribution, concentration, and the liquid in which the sand is carried all enter a settling test, and none of them enters a vendor rule. The plan area of 294 m2 is therefore the area the vendor basis gives, and a settling test on the actual slurry is the measurement that would confirm or move it.
